MOD_PLAN.md section 6 item 42 (LEADS.md Part J, kindi checkpoint_every), STRATA_CKPT_STRIDE=N (default off, state placement only: exact text). A request that resumed at R takes its periodic checkpoints at R+N, R+2N, R+3N (STRATA_CKPT_STRIDE_MAX, default 3) instead of every --prompt-cache-every (16384) tokens, so a later request that edits the middle of the prefix resumes from the nearest checkpoint below the edit. Rule: include/strata/program/ckpt_stride.hpp (host test ckpt_stride_test, T-727). THE TEST THAT MATTERS is the mid-prefix edit: python3 tools/pancake/mid_edit_bench.py --port

--label base --out mid-base.json on an engine started with the base command, then again with STRATA_CKPT_STRIDE=4096 (--label stride4k) and python3 tools/pancake/mid_edit_bench.py --compare mid-base.json mid-stride4k.json: per edit position (25/50/75% of a 32K conversation) the reused tokens, the tokens read again and TTFT; 3 rounds each (pytest tools/pancake/test_mid_edit_bench.py, T-728). The abtest screen (python3 tools/pancake/abtest.py bench/specs/142-ckpt-stride.json --tier screen) shows only the COST of the extra checkpoints (each is a 112.2 MiB GDN copy, STRATA_TRACE prints 'checkpoint at N: sync X ms, save Y ms'; long3k reads 3K tokens so the stride arms add 0-1 checkpoint there). It pays only when turns diverge inside the prefix; the share of such requests is NOT recorded (M3 not recorded), so a gain on mid_edit_bench is an upper bound for real traffic. The extra checkpoints share the --prompt-cache slots (6): read the root / turn checkpoints' survival in the log. NOT MEASURED (queued).
